title: Two Algorithms for Orthogonal Nonnegative Matrix Factorization with Application to Clustering

citations.claim: Pompili et al. proved that orthogonal NMF is mathematically equivalent to a weighted variant of spherical k-means clustering.

Pompili et al. proposed ONP-MF, an augmented Lagrangian method that strictly enforces orthogonality at each iteration while relaxing nonnegativity via a quadratic penalty, reversing the strategy of standard ONMF algorithms that enforce nonnegativity while pursuing orthogonality asymptotically.

Pompili et al. showed that the nonnegativity and orthogonality constraints together imply that each column of the factor V has at most one nonzero entry, giving ONMF an inherent hard-clustering interpretation.

Pompili et al. demonstrated that ONP-MF can be initialized with unaltered right singular vectors from SVD, which is impossible with other ONMF methods that require nonnegative initialization, and this deterministic initialization contributed to superior clustering performance.

Pompili et al. showed experimentally that ONP-MF outperformed other ONMF algorithms on hyperspectral unmixing tasks, being the only method to successfully recover all constituent materials in a synthetic Hubble telescope dataset.

do_not_claim: Pompili et al. applied ONMF to signal denoising, baseline correction, or chromatography
Pompili et al. proposed deep learning or neural network methods
Pompili et al. addressed the problem of algorithm unrolling or deep unfolding
